title.narrative: Promoting MIL through Policy Support and Capacity building for Stakeholders

description.narrative:
South Sudan is an oral society but is now on the transition to developing its media and ICT sector. South Sudan media is underdeveloped in the region and the landscape is changing rapidly hence more consumption of media content. The literacy rate in South Sudan is so low compared to its neighbors. The effect of long wars in South Sudan had great negative impact on education. For example, the literacy rate according to UNESCO is 34.52% adults. Male literacy is 40.26%; Female 28.86%; Youth is about 44.35% between ages 15-24. Lowest literacy rate compared to its neighbors. In addition, South Sudan does not have a comprehensive Media and Information Literacy (MIL) policy and strategy. It can, therefore, be said that South Sudan is currently in the process of designing a comprehensive Media and Information Literacy for its further development. However, some aspects of Media and Information Literacy (MIL) concepts of various literacies are recognized in different policy and strategic documents in South Sudan
Interventions on Media and Information Literacy in South Sudan is aimed at empowering beneficiaries/ citizens with skills of critical thinking and creative problem solving and to make them become informed consumers as well as information producers. Facilitates South Sudanese citizens to become smarter and productive participants of development discourses by using media effectively and interacting actively with and through media and information. Also, the proposed Interventions on MIL for South Sudan is intended to empower South Sudanese citizens on harnessing the benefit of the effective use of media and ICTs.
Part of progress achieved for South Sudan is the development of a draft MIL Policy and strategy document and Draft Curriculum on MIL for educators and Trainers. The proposed efforts will further the efforts that have been supported through policy support and capacity building.
